title: Concession and contrast
objectives: Use kahit (na) and bagaman to concede a point within a sentence
Link opposing sentences with gayunpaman, sa kabila nito and samantala
Replace a rejected alternative with sa halip (na)
Build multi-clause argumentative sentences that concede, contrast, and conclude

grammar.title: kahit (na) and bagaman: conceding inside the sentence
grammar.explanation:
Kahit (na) 'even though / even if' is the everyday concessive: Kahit pagod siya, pumasok pa rin siya sa trabaho — 'Even though she was tired, she still went to work.' Note the pa rin ('still') that so often answers a kahit-clause; the pair kahit... pa rin is the skeleton of countless Tagalog sentences. Kahit also builds indefinites you already half-know: kahit sino 'anyone', kahit ano 'anything', kahit kailan 'ever', kahit saan 'anywhere'.

Bagaman (also spelled bagama't with the fused at) is the formal, written counterpart: Bagaman maliit ang kanyang sahod, nakapagpatapos siya ng tatlong anak — 'Although his salary was small, he put three children through school.' You will meet bagaman constantly in editorials and reports, rarely in casual talk. Its casual paraphrase is simply kahit na.

Both clauses can come in either order. When the concessive clause comes second, it often carries a softening effect: Maganda ang plano, kahit na may ilang butas — 'The plan is good, even if it has some holes.'

grammar.title: gayunpaman, sa kabila ng, samantala: contrast across sentences
grammar.explanation:
To pivot between whole sentences, formal Tagalog uses gayunpaman 'nevertheless, even so' (also gayunman, sa kabila nito): Bumagsak ang benta ngayong taon. Gayunpaman, hindi nagtanggal ng empleyado ang kompanya — 'Sales fell this year. Nevertheless, the company laid off no employees.'

Sa kabila ng + noun phrase is 'despite / in spite of': Sa kabila ng ulan, tuloy ang laro — 'Despite the rain, the game goes on.' With a full clause, wrap it in nominalized form or use sa kabila ng katotohanang... 'despite the fact that...'. Its cousin sa kabila nito 'despite this' points back at the previous sentence.

Samantala as a sentence-opener means 'meanwhile', switching scenes or contrasting two ongoing situations: Nagdiriwang ang mga nanalo. Samantala, tahimik na umuwi ang mga natalo. As samantalang inside one sentence it means 'while/whereas' and often carries reproach at inequality: Nagtatapon sila ng pagkain, samantalang nagugutom ang iba — 'They throw food away, while others go hungry.'

grammar.title: sa halip and building the concede-then-counter move
grammar.explanation:
Sa halip na + verb/clause means 'instead of': Sa halip na magreklamo, kumilos siya — 'Instead of complaining, he acted.' As a sentence-opener, Sa halip, ... means 'Instead, ...': Hindi siya sumagot. Sa halip, tumayo siya at umalis.

Now assemble the B2 argumentative move you'll need in debate and essays — concede, then counter, then conclude: (1) concede with totoo na / aminado ako na / bagaman: Totoo na mahal ang solar panels. (2) counter with pero / gayunpaman / sa kabila nito: Gayunpaman, mas mura ito sa katagalan. (3) conclude with kaya / samakatuwid: Kaya sulit pa rin ang pagbili nito.

One warning about ngunit and subalit: both mean 'but' in writing (ngunit slightly more common, subalit the most formal); in speech, people just say pero or kaso. Choosing ngunit in conversation sounds like reading aloud from a book — a register mismatch you now know how to avoid.

vocab.note: also spelled bagama't; casual equivalent is kahit na

example.tl: Bagaman matanda na siya, malakas pa rin ang kanyang boses.
example.en: Although he is old, his voice is still strong.

vocab.note: sentence-opener; variants gayunman, sa kabila nito

example.tl: Mahirap ang pagsusulit. Gayunpaman, marami pa ring pumasa.
example.en: The exam was hard. Nevertheless, many still passed.

vocab.note: followed by a noun phrase; 'sa kabila nito' = despite this

example.tl: Sa kabila ng init, dinumog ng tao ang parada.
example.en: Despite the heat, people flocked to the parade.

example.tl: Naglilinis ang mga bata. Samantala, nagluluto ang kanilang ina.
example.en: The children are cleaning. Meanwhile, their mother is cooking.

example.tl: Malaki ang bahay nila, samantalang maliit ang sa amin.
example.en: Their house is big, whereas ours is small.

example.tl: Sa halip na mag-taxi, naglakad na lang kami.
example.en: Instead of taking a taxi, we just walked.

example.tl: Gusto niyang sumama, ngunit may lagnat siya.
example.en: She wanted to come along, but she had a fever.

example.tl: Nangako ang opisyal, subalit walang nangyari.
example.en: The official made promises, but nothing happened.

vocab.note: aminado ako na... = I admit that...

example.tl: Aminado akong nagkamali ako sa una kong sagot.
example.en: I admit I was wrong in my first answer.

example.tl: Totoo na mahal ito, pero matibay naman.
example.en: It's true this is expensive, but it is durable.

example.tl: Walang ebidensya. Samakatuwid, hindi siya maaaring hatulan.
example.en: There is no evidence. Therefore, he cannot be convicted.

example.tl: Magkasalungat ang kanilang opinyon tungkol sa batas.
example.en: Their opinions about the law are opposed.

example.tl: Sinalungat ng konsehal ang panukala ng alkalde.
example.en: The councilor opposed the mayor's proposal.

vocab.note: kumampi sa panig = to side with

example.tl: Pakinggan natin ang magkabilang panig bago magpasya.
example.en: Let's hear both sides before deciding.

example.tl: Ayaw niyang pumanig sa alinmang grupo.
example.en: He doesn't want to side with any group.

example.tl: Nagpumilit siyang umuwi kahit malakas ang ulan.
example.en: He insisted on going home even though the rain was heavy.

example.tl: Sumang-ayon ang karamihan sa bagong patakaran.
example.en: The majority agreed with the new policy.

example.tl: Tumutol ang mga residente sa pagtatayo ng planta.
example.en: The residents objected to the construction of the plant.

example.tl: Ipinatupad ang bagong patakaran sa parking noong Lunes.
example.en: The new parking policy was implemented on Monday.

example.tl: Pinag-aaralan pa ng konseho ang panukala.
example.en: The council is still studying the proposal.

example.tl: Ano ang kalamangan ng pag-aaral sa ibang bansa?
example.en: What is the advantage of studying abroad?

example.tl: Kahinaan ng plano ang laki ng gastos.
example.en: The plan's weakness is the size of the cost.

example.tl: Matibay ang kanyang argumento dahil may datos siya.
example.en: Her argument is strong because she has data.

example.tl: Maraming butas ang paliwanag ng testigo.
example.en: The witness's explanation has many holes.

vocab.note: sa katagalan = in the long run

example.tl: Mas makakatipid ka sa katagalan kung bibili ka ng de-kalidad.
example.en: You'll save more in the long run if you buy quality.

vocab.en: to be able to save (money, time)

example.tl: Nakatipid kami nang malaki nang lumipat kami ng apartment.
example.en: We saved a lot when we moved apartments.

vocab.note: from dumog; usually seen in completed form in news

example.tl: Dinumog ng mga tagahanga ang aktor sa mall.
example.en: Fans mobbed the actor at the mall.

dialogue.title: Dapat bang bawal ang cellphone sa klase?
dialogue.context: Teachers Lorna and Jun disagree during a faculty meeting about a proposed classroom phone ban.

lines.speaker: Lorna
lines.tl: Sang-ayon ako sa panukala. Kahit anong gawin natin, nakatingin lang sa cellphone ang mga estudyante.
lines.en: I agree with the proposal. No matter what we do, the students just stare at their phones.

lines.speaker: Jun
lines.tl: Totoo na nakakaabala ang cellphone. Gayunpaman, hindi solusyon ang tuluyang pagbabawal.
lines.en: It's true that phones are distracting. Nevertheless, a total ban is not the solution.

lines.speaker: Lorna
lines.tl: Bakit hindi? Sa ibang paaralan, tumaas ang grado nang ipinagbawal ito.
lines.en: Why not? In other schools, grades went up when it was banned.

lines.speaker: Jun
lines.tl: Bagaman totoo iyan, iba ang kalagayan natin. Maraming estudyante natin ang gumagamit ng cellphone bilang diksyunaryo at calculator.
lines.en: Although that's true, our situation is different. Many of our students use their phones as a dictionary and calculator.

lines.speaker: Lorna
lines.tl: E di bumili sila ng totoong diksyunaryo.
lines.en: Then let them buy a real dictionary.

lines.speaker: Jun
lines.tl: Sa kabila ng mababang presyo ng lumang diksyunaryo, hindi pa rin iyon kayang bilhin ng iba. Samantalang may cellphone na sila.
lines.en: Despite the low price of an old dictionary, some still can't afford one. Whereas they already have phones.

lines.speaker: Lorna
lines.tl: May punto ka. Pero paano natin mapipigilan ang paglalaro nila habang nagklaklase?
lines.en: You have a point. But how do we stop them from playing games during class?

lines.speaker: Jun
lines.tl: Sa halip na tuluyang pagbabawal, maglagay tayo ng malinaw na patakaran: nakasilid ang cellphone maliban kung sinabi ng guro.
lines.en: Instead of a total ban, let's set a clear policy: phones stay put away unless the teacher says otherwise.

lines.speaker: Lorna
lines.tl: Hmm. Aminado akong mas makatwiran iyan kaysa sa panukala ko.
lines.en: Hmm. I admit that's more reasonable than my proposal.

lines.speaker: Jun
lines.tl: Samakatuwid, magkasundo tayo: may patakaran, pero walang tuluyang pagbabawal.
lines.en: Therefore, we agree: there's a policy, but no total ban.

lines.speaker: Lorna
lines.tl: Sige. Isusulat ko ang bersyong iyan para sa botohan sa susunod na pulong.
lines.en: Alright. I'll write up that version for the vote at the next meeting.

reading.title: Ang lungsod na ayaw matulog
reading.tl:
Tanyag ang Lungsod ng Baguio bilang tahimik na destinasyon para sa mga pagod na taga-Maynila. Malamig ang hangin, luntian ang mga puno ng pino, at mabagal ang takbo ng buhay. Gayunpaman, iba na ang Baguio tuwing kapaskuhan.

Sa kabila ng limitadong mga kalsada nito, pumapasok sa lungsod ang libu-libong sasakyan bawat araw ng Disyembre. Puno ang mga otel, dinudumog ang mga parke, at ang dating dalawampung minutong biyahe ay umaabot ng dalawang oras. Bagaman malaki ang kinikita ng mga negosyo, dumaraing naman ang mga residente: mahal na ang bilihin, maingay na ang mga gabi, at nagkalat na ang basura sa mga bangketa.

Magkasalungat ang panig ng mga taga-Baguio mismo. Sabi ng mga may-ari ng tindahan at otel, buhay ng lungsod ang turismo; kung mawawala ito, mawawalan ng trabaho ang marami. Samantala, iginigiit ng ibang residente na hindi lahat ng kita ay katumbas ng kapayapaan ng isang pamayanan. "Sa halip na dagdagan pa ang mga bisita," sabi ng isang guro na tumutol sa bagong festival, "dapat munang ayusin ang basura at trapiko."

Ngayong taon, sinusubukan ng pamahalaang lokal ang gitnang landas: limitadong bilang ng sasakyang papasok, mas mataas na bayad sa parking, at mas mahigpit na patakaran sa basura. Maagang sabihin kung magtatagumpay ito. Ngunit isang bagay ang malinaw: kahit pagod na ang Baguio, hindi pa rin ito pinababayaang matulog ng mga panauhin nito.
reading.en:
Baguio City is famous as a quiet destination for tired Manila folk. The air is cold, the pine trees are green, and the pace of life is slow. Nevertheless, Baguio is a different place every Christmas season.

Despite its limited roads, thousands of vehicles enter the city every day in December. The hotels are full, the parks are mobbed, and what used to be a twenty-minute trip stretches to two hours. Although businesses earn a great deal, residents complain: goods have become expensive, the nights are noisy, and trash is scattered on the sidewalks.

Baguio's own people are on opposing sides. The shop and hotel owners say tourism is the city's lifeblood; if it disappears, many will lose their jobs. Meanwhile, other residents insist that not all income is worth a community's peace. "Instead of adding even more visitors," said a teacher who opposed the new festival, "the trash and traffic should be fixed first."

This year, the local government is trying a middle path: a limited number of vehicles allowed in, higher parking fees, and stricter rules on garbage. It is too early to say whether it will succeed. But one thing is clear: even though Baguio is tired, its guests still won't let it sleep.

exercises.prompt: Which connector is the formal written equivalent of 'kahit na'?
exercises.explain: Bagaman (bagama't) is the written-register 'although'. Samantala is 'meanwhile', sa halip 'instead', samakatuwid 'therefore'.

exercises.prompt: Bumagsak ang negosyo nila. ___, hindi sila sumuko. (Nevertheless)
exercises.explain: Gayunpaman (or gayunman / sa kabila nito) pivots between sentences: 'Their business collapsed. Nevertheless, they didn't give up.'

exercises.prompt: Sa kabila ___ mataas na lagnat, pumasok pa rin siya. Which word completes it?
exercises.explain: Sa kabila ng takes a noun phrase: sa kabila ng mataas na lagnat 'despite the high fever'.

exercises.prompt: Nagtatapon sila ng tubig, samantalang walang mainom ang ibang barangay. What does samantalang signal here?
choices: a time sequence: first one event, then the other
a reproachful contrast between two simultaneous situations
exercises.explain: Mid-sentence samantalang means 'while/whereas' and often carries reproach at an unfair contrast: wasting water while others have none to drink.

exercises.prompt: ___ na magreklamo sa social media, pumunta siya mismo sa opisina. (Instead of)
exercises.explain: Sa halip na + verb = 'instead of doing X'. Colloquial speech also uses imbes na; sa halip is the written norm.

exercises.tl: Bagaman maliit ang kanilang puhunan, lumago ang negosyo nila sa loob ng dalawang taon.
choices: Although their capital was small, their business grew within two years.
Because their capital was small, their business failed in two years.
Their large capital made the business grow for two years.
They borrowed capital to grow the business for two years.
exercises.explain: Bagaman concedes the small capital (puhunan); the main clause reports the growth anyway. No cause-effect or failure is stated.

exercises.prompt: Even though the ticket is expensive, I will still watch the game.
exercises.answer: Kahit na mahal ang tiket, manonood pa rin ako ng laro.
accept: Kahit na mahal ang tiket, manonood pa rin ako ng laro
Kahit mahal ang tiket, manonood pa rin ako ng laro
Manonood pa rin ako ng laro kahit mahal ang tiket
exercises.explain: Kahit (na) concedes; pa rin 'still' in the main clause completes the classic kahit... pa rin frame.

exercises.prompt: Totoo na malayo ang lakad, pero sulit naman ang tanawin sa taas.
exercises.answer: It's true that the hike is long, but the view at the top is worth it.
accept: It's true that the hike is long, but the view at the top is worth it
It is true the walk is far, but the view up top is worth it
True, the hike is long, but the view at the top makes it worth it
exercises.explain: Totoo na... pero... is the concede-then-counter frame: concede the distance, counter with the payoff (sulit 'worth it').

exercises.prompt: You are chatting casually with a friend. Which 'but' fits the register?
exercises.explain: Pero (or kaso) is the spoken 'but'. Ngunit and subalit belong to writing; using them in chat sounds like reading from a book.

exercises.prompt: Walang sapat na ebidensya laban sa kanya. ___, dapat siyang pawalang-sala. (Therefore)
exercises.explain: Samakatuwid draws the formal conclusion; kaya is its everyday equivalent. The concede-counter-conclude chain ends with a connector like this.

exercises.tl: Sa kabila ng pagtutol ng ilang residente, ipinasa pa rin ng konseho ang panukala kagabi.
choices: The council passed the proposal despite some residents' objections.
The residents passed a proposal against the council.
The council rejected the proposal because residents objected.
The council postponed the vote out of respect for the residents.
exercises.explain: Sa kabila ng pagtutol = 'despite the objection'; ipinasa pa rin = 'still passed it'. The concession did not stop the vote.

exercises.prompt: I admit the plan has holes. Nevertheless, it is better than doing nothing.
exercises.answer: Aminado akong may mga butas ang plano. Gayunpaman, mas mabuti ito kaysa sa walang gawin.
accept: Aminado akong may mga butas ang plano. Gayunpaman, mas mabuti ito kaysa sa walang gawin
Aminado ako na may mga butas ang plano. Gayunpaman, mas mabuti ito kaysa walang gawin
Aminado akong may butas ang plano. Gayunpaman, mas mabuti ito kaysa sa wala
exercises.explain: Aminado ako na... opens the concession; gayunpaman executes the counter. Butas 'holes/flaws' is the unit's figurative noun for weaknesses in an argument.
